# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 36 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_036_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Chapter 2 — How to Discern the Two Angels

**1** "I asked him, "Sir, how will I know which spirit comes from God and which is devilish?" **2** "Listen," he said, "and I will tell you about both spirits, and you may test them by what I say. **3** The spirit that comes from God is long-suffering, peaceful, modest, abstaining from all wickedness and vain desire of this age, making itself humble before all men, quieting itself, not quarreling with anyone at all, not putting itself forward, nor yet being too bold in speaking — it speaks through peace and gentleness. **4** This one pleases God. When therefore this spirit enters your heart, speak with it on those things that are righteous. For where the Lord dwells he does not dwell in the realm of deception; but where God is, there is also great understanding. Trust therefore the spirit which comes from God and has power, but do not trust the spirit from the devil at all, for it has no power." **5** "And what is the power of the spirit which comes from God, and what is the power of the spirit from the devil?" **6** He said: "The spirit from the devil has no power, and it is weak like winter grass; it is foolish and not worthy of trust. Now when the earthly spirit has no power it becomes like a winter vegetable and withers away. **7** But the spirit from God that has power in it is zealous in strength and of upright character — it is trustworthy and does not doubt. When this spirit enters your heart, speak with it about righteousness, justice, and holiness."

---

*EMET note: Mandate 6.2 — the discernment test. The spirit from God = long-suffering, peaceful, humble, gentle-speaking. The spirit from the devil = has no power, like winter grass (withers). The discernment is by the character of the inner states produced.*
